**Dynasty:** 陳
**Date:** 558–569

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A single-fascicle treatise on the eighteen modes of emptiness (*aṣṭādaśa-śūnyatā*) — a standard analytical scheme drawn from the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* literature and absorbed into Yogācāra through the *Yogācārabhūmi* and the *Madhyāntavibhāga*. The Chinese catalog attributes the work to [龍樹菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BE%8D%E6%A8%B9%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Nāgārjuna), but the modern critical literature regards this attribution as pseudepigraphic: the text is in fact an excerpt from the *Madhyāntavibhāga* corpus or its sub-commentaries, abstracted and translated separately by [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6).

**Abstract**

The Nāgārjuna attribution preserved in the catalog is not credible: the Sanskrit source is unknown, the text is not in the Tibetan canon, and the doctrinal framework is straightforwardly Yogācāra (it analyses the eighteen *śūnyatā* in terms of *trisvabhāva* and *vijñapti-mātratā*, not in *Madhyamaka* terms). The work is best understood as an excerpt from a now-lost Indian Yogācāra commentary on the *Madhyāntavibhāga* — possibly Sthiramati's *Madhyāntavibhāgaṭīkā* — translated separately by Paramārtha for didactic purposes during his Chén-period activity (558–569).

The dating bracket adopted (558–569) reflects the standard window for Paramārtha's Chén-period southern translation activity. The pseudepigraphic attribution to Nāgārjuna is presumably intended to lend authority to the topic of *śūnyatā*, which in Chinese Buddhist culture had become firmly identified with the Mādhyamika master.

The eighteen-fold *śūnyatā* scheme is one of the principal didactic frameworks for Yogācāra emptiness-doctrine and is treated extensively in [KR6n0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0001) *Yújiā shī dì lùn* and the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* commentarial tradition.
